changes: Explicitly opted-in diagnostics require frozen targets, tool hashes, original role receipt and exact private node ownership.
Record public route source and before/after kelinode PID/network-namespace context; source or namespace mismatch suppresses extra echo requests.
Bound and merge ping stdout/stderr; distinguish valid echoes, no echo by deadline, returned ICMP errors, permission/bind/route errors and process/output failures.
Read-only nft snapshots retain hashed chain/rule references, hook/priority/policy, rule position/verdict, literal receipt-address membership and counters without raw rule/config text.
Counter deltas require unchanged structure and nondecreasing counters; reset, named, missing or unreadable counters remain unknown, not zero.
Read fixed procfs ICMP counters with a byte cap instead of trusting their virtual zero file size; shared counters are not individual packet attribution.
An exclusive intent prevents diagnostic replay; closed/deleting/expired contexts refuse contact, and existing stop requests suppress active ICMP.
The fresh driver's baseline-failure branch may collect once before writing stop, while the later cleanup adapter preserves the first report and never reprobes.
Diagnostics, transport and persistence failures cannot suppress or retry original cleanup; summaries never change acceptance or confirm censorship.

local_validation.command: python -B -m unittest -q test_staging test_bootstrap_diagnostics test_diagnostic_capture test_entry_probe_diagnostics test_entry_probe_capture test_driver_journal test_install_only_runner test_worker.WorkerTests test_driver_linux test_application_bundle

limits: Windows fixtures and mocks do not establish real Linux capability, namespace, nft, procfs or pipe-lifecycle behavior.
The nft outline is not a complete rule evaluator; literal address membership does not mean the whole rule matched or establish effective allow/drop.
Named sets/maps, regular-chain direction and other conditions remain unmodelled. Legacy iptables, XDP/eBPF, provider and transit filters are not evaluated.
Rule and host counters are shared with other traffic and cannot attribute individual diagnostic packets or prove a drop location.
A stopped branch receives only passive diagnostics; fresh ICMP error evidence requires the new reviewed driver to call capture before its stop intent.
This does not recover R10's deleted source or historical packets, confirm censorship, or pass WAN/HY2/DNS failover acceptance.
Linux CI and any new live acceptance need separate execution; no historical campaign is patched or resumed.
